newsitem.title: THAILAND: Japanese firms urge caution on Thai minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms urge caution on Thai minimum wage.

text.p: Three Bangkok-based Japanese firms have urged Thailand to respond cautiously to calls for a rise in the daily minimum wage for unskilled workers, a Labour Ministry official said on Wednesday.
Labour unions are demanding a 20-baht rise in the minimum wage for workers in Bangkok and five neighbouring provinces, which is currently 157 baht ($6.04) a day.

The chairmen of Sanyo Semiconductor (Thailand) Co Ltd, TDK (Thailand) Co Ltd and Honda Cars Manufacturing (Thailand) Co Ltd made their appeal in a joint letter which was sent to Minister of Labour and Social Welfare Chatchai Eartrakul on Monday.
The ministry official said the three companies were concerned that a rise in the daily minimum wage would affect production costs and competitiveness of Thai exports.
The official said the companies also called for government intervention to solve any future labour disputes.

Workers at Sanyo Universal Electric Plc burned down the company's warehouse on the outskirts of Bangkok last December after a decline in the company's earnings led to a reduction in annual bonuses. ($1 = 26 baht)
